country.comment: Conducted in urban slums of Ludhiana City, Punjab, North India.
country.where_found: PDF p. 1, Title and Abstract; PDF p. 3, Section II

effect_estimate.comment: Although Section III.g states that odds ratios and 95% CIs were calculated where appropriate, only frequencies, percentages, and chi-square test statistics/p-values (grouping open spaces with non-notified slums) are reported in the results tables.
effect_estimate.value: Across 3,947 newer migrant households, 37.2% (1,468/3,947) had in-house piped water, 37.5% (1,480) used a public tap, 20.2% (797) used a hand pump, and 5.1% (202) had no water supply; 29.8% (1,178/3,947) had a home toilet while 57.2% (2,256) practised open defecation; and 43.0% (1,696) had closed drains while 17.7% (697) had no drainage. Access differed significantly across notified slums (n = 845), non-notified slums (n = 3,072), and open spaces (n = 30, pooled with non-notified slums for chi-square tests): drinking water source (chi-square = 155.36, df = 6, p = 0.000001; piped water at home: 45.4% in notified vs. 35.3% in non-notified and 0% in open spaces; no water supply: 1.9% vs. 5.8% and 26.7%), defecation facility (chi-square = 163.29, df = 3, p = 0.000001; own toilet at home: 43.2% in notified vs. 26.5% in non-notified and 0% in open spaces; open defecation: 54.7% vs. 57.6% and 83.3%), and drainage (chi-square = 116.02, df = 4, p = 0.000001; closed drain: 55.7% in notified vs. 39.7% in non-notified and 20.0% in open spaces). Additionally, 96.9% (3,823/3,947) lacked a voter card (chi-square = 4.51, df = 1, p = 0.033695) and 96.2% (3,798/3,947) lacked a ration card (chi-square = 3.31, df = 2, p = 0.191516). No odds ratios or confidence intervals were reported.
effect_estimate.where_found: PDF p. 7, Section IV; PDF pp. 8–9, Tables 3 and 4

mechanism_certainty.comment: Cross-sectional survey (capped at <= 2) documenting a statistically significant bivariate association (via chi-square tests) between legal slum notification status and household water, sanitation, and drainage availability, as well as descriptive prevalence of missing identity/residence documents and tenancy, while relying on secondary literature rather than direct empirical observation of municipal application or administrative decision-making processes to explain institutional bottlenecks.
mechanism_certainty.where_found: PDF pp. 8–11, Tables 2–4 and Section V

mechanism_flags.comment: Examines formal slum notification under Slum Acts vs. non-notified slums and open spaces (determining municipal legal obligation to provide services), phased municipal recognition/provision to non-notified slums, household tenancy/ownership and ambiguity over land ownership and permissible land uses, unplanned urban growth, and lack of government proof of identity/residence (voter and ration cards, birth registration).
mechanism_flags.value: ELIGIBILITY, DISCRETION_ACCOMMODATION, tenure, documentation, property, planning, zoning, service_area, accommodation
mechanism_flags.where_found: PDF p. 3, Section II.a; PDF p. 6, Section III.f; PDF pp. 8–11, Tables 2–4 and Section V

outcome_flags.comment: Measures household drinking water access (in-house piped water, public tap, hand pump, no supply), sanitation and drainage access (home/community/mobile toilet vs. open defecation; closed/open/no drains), formal vs. unauthorized connections, and notes intermittent piped water continuity (1–2 hours morning and evening).
outcome_flags.where_found: PDF p. 7, Section IV; PDF pp. 9–11, Table 4 and Section V

publication_year.comment: Published in Environment & Urbanization Vol 28(2), October 2016.
publication_year.where_found: PDF p. 1, journal header and footer; PDF p. 2, running header

risk_of_bias_tool.comment: Quantitative observational cross-sectional household survey comparing civic amenity availability across notified slums, non-notified slums, and open spaces using chi-square tests without a quasi-experimental intervention design.
risk_of_bias_tool.value: JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Analytical Cross Sectional Studies
risk_of_bias_tool.where_found: PDF p. 3, Section II; PDF pp. 4–6, Section III

sample_size.comment: Sampled from a benchmark frame of 91 slums (50 notified, 41 non-notified); total population in the 30 sampled slum clusters was 91,486 individuals in 17,342 households, from which 3,947 newer migrant households (migrated >30 days and <10 years ago) were surveyed.
sample_size.value: 3,947 newer migrant households across 30 slum settlements (845 households in 15 notified slums; 3,102 households in 15 non-notified slums, comprising 3,072 in non-notified slums and 30 in open spaces)
sample_size.where_found: PDF p. 1, Abstract; PDF p. 4, Section III; PDF p. 5, Section III.c; PDF p. 6, Table 1; PDF pp. 8–9, Tables 2–4

study_design.comment: Data collected between 1 August 2011 and 31 July 2014 via household survey interviews with heads of families.
study_design.value: Cross-sectional household survey (simple random sample of 15 notified and 15 non-notified slum settlements, with purposive and snowball sampling of newer migrant households, analysed using chi-square tests)
study_design.where_found: PDF p. 1, Abstract; PDF p. 3, Section II; PDF pp. 4–6, Section III
